node_mito_membranes_import.title: Mitochondrial Membranes (Cardiolipin) & Post-Translational Protein Import (TOM / TIM23 / TIM22)
node_mito_membranes_import.subtitle: Porin-Permeable OMM vs. Impermeable Cristae IMM | Amphipathic N-Terminal Matrix Targeting Presequences

metrics.outer_membrane_omm: 40% Lipid : 60% Protein; contains VDAC (Porin) channels permeable to molecules <5,000 Da (IMS pH = Cytosol pH ~7.2!)
metrics.inner_membrane_imm: 20% Lipid : 80% Protein; enriched in Cardiolipin (Diphosphatidylglycerol — 4 acyl chains!); 100% impermeable to H+, K+, Cl-, NADH
metrics.matrix_import_tim23: N-terminal amphipathic α-helix (positively charged) -> TOM40 -> TIM23/TIM44 + mtHsp70 (Requires BOTH ΔΨ across IMM AND Matrix ATP!)
metrics.carrier_import_tim22: Internal targeting sequences (no cleavable presequence, e.g., ANT) -> Cytosolic Hsp70/90 -> TOM -> Small Tim9/10 -> TIM22 (Requires ΔΨ ONLY!)

mechanism: **1. COMPARTMENTALIZATION & THE CARDIOLIPIN SEAL**:

• The **Outer Mitochondrial Membrane (OMM)** contains abundant **VDAC (Voltage-Dependent Anion Channel / Porin)** beta-barrels, making the **Intermembrane Space (IMS)** chemically equivalent to the cytosol for small ions and metabolites ($<5\ \text{kDa}$).

• The **Inner Mitochondrial Membrane (IMM)**—folded into **Cristae** by **MICOS** and **OPA1** complexes—contains **~20% Cardiolipin (diphosphatidylglycerol)**, a unique dimeric phospholipid with four fatty acyl chains that packs tightly around respiratory complexes and makes the IMM virtually **100% impermeable to protons ($\text{H}^+$)**, enabling maintenance of a $-180\ \text{mV}$ membrane potential.
**2. POST-TRANSLATIONAL PROTEIN IMPORT (>99% of Mitochondrial Proteins are Nuclear-Encoded!)**:
• Precursor proteins are synthesized on **free cytosolic polysomes** and kept unfolded by **cytosolic Hsp70** (requiring cytosolic ATP hydrolysis to release!).

• **Matrix-Targeted Proteins (TOM $\rightarrow$ TIM23 Pathway)**: Carry a cleavable N-terminal **amphipathic $\alpha$-helix presequence** (positively charged Arg/Lys on one face, hydrophobic on the other). Recognized by **Tom20/Tom22**, threaded through **Tom40** and **Tim23**, driven across the IMM by **electrophoretic attraction of the positive presequence to the negative Matrix ($\Delta\Psi$)** AND pulled in by the **PAM motor (mtHsp70 + Tim44, which hydrolyzes Matrix ATP)**, before cleavage by **MPP (Mitochondrial Processing Peptidase)**!
csir_high_yield: Guaranteed CSIR NET Part C Experimental Questions on Mitochondrial Import Energetics:
• **What happens to Matrix Protein Import if you add Valinomycin/DNP (collapsing $\Delta\Psi$) vs. Oligomycin/Atractyloside (depleting Matrix ATP)?**
– **Collapsing $\Delta\Psi$ across the IMM**: Completely abolishes insertion of the positively charged presequence into **TIM23** AND abolishes carrier insertion into **TIM22**!

– **Depleting Matrix ATP (while keeping $\Delta\Psi$ intact)**: The N-terminal presequence STILL crosses the IMM via TIM23 (driven by $\Delta\Psi$) and gets cleaved by MPP, **BUT the rest of the polypeptide stalls halfway across the membrane** because **mtHsp70** requires Matrix ATP to ratchet the protein inside!
• **Intermembrane Space (IMS) Routing via the 'Stop-Transfer' vs. 'MIA40 Disulfide Relay'**:

– **Cytochrome $b_2$ / Cytochrome $c_1$**: Carry a **bipartite signal** (matrix targeting sequence followed immediately by a hydrophobic stop-transfer sequence that arrests in TIM23 and is cleaved by inner-membrane peptidase **Imp1** to release the mature protein into the IMS!).
pathology: **Barth Syndrome**: X-linked mutation in the **TAZ (*Tafazzin*)** gene (a phospholipid transacylase that remodels cardiolipin acyl chains) causes cardiolipin deficiency, destabilizing ETC supercomplexes and leading to dilated cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, and skeletal myopathy.
lab_workbench: Isolated Mitochondria Proteinase K Protection + MPP Cleavage Assay: Incubating isolated mitochondria with radiolabeled $^{35}\text{S}$-precursor protein in vitro: successful import into the matrix is proved by (1) shift to a smaller MW band (**MPP cleavage of presequence**) AND (2) **complete resistance to externally added Proteinase K** (unless Triton X-100 detergent is added to lyse the membranes!).

metrics.pdh_5_cofactors: TPP (Vit B1, E1), Lipoamide (E2), Coenzyme A (Vit B5, E2), FAD (Vit B2, E3), NAD+ (Vit B3, E3)

metrics.malate_aspartate_shuttle: Liver, Kidney & Heart: Cytosolic NADH -> Matrix NADH (Complex I) -> Yields 2.5 ATP per cytosolic NADH -> Total = 32 ATP / Glucose!
metrics.glycerol_3p_shuttle: Skeletal Muscle & Brain: Cytosolic NADH -> Mitochondrial FAD-G3PDH -> Ubiquinone (Bypasses Complex I!) -> Yields 1.5 ATP -> Total = 30 ATP / Glucose!

mechanism: Because the Inner Mitochondrial Membrane is **100% impermeable to cytosolic NADH** (generated during glycolysis by GAPDH), reducing equivalents must be ferried into the electron transport chain via one of two tissue-specific **Substrate Shuttles**:

1. **MALATE–ASPARTATE SHUTTLE (Reversible; Heart, Liver, Kidney — Zero Energetic Loss!)**: Cytosolic **Malate Dehydrogenase (cMDH)** reduces Oxaloacetate (OAA) + $\text{NADH} \rightarrow$ **Malate** + $\text{NAD}^+$. Malate enters the matrix via the **Malate–$\alpha$-Ketoglutarate Antiporter** and is re-oxidized by mitochondrial **mMDH** back into OAA + **Matrix NADH** (which enters **Complex I**, yielding **2.5 ATP**!). Matrix OAA is transaminated to **Aspartate**, which exits via the electrogenic **Glutamate–Aspartate Antiporter**.

2. **GLYCEROL-3-PHOSPHATE SHUTTLE (Irreversible; Skeletal Muscle, Brain, Insect Flight Muscle — Fast but Costs 1 ATP!)**: Cytosolic G3PDH reduces DHAP + $\text{NADH} \rightarrow$ **Glycerol-3-Phosphate**, which is oxidized on the outer face of the IMM by **flavoprotein mG3PDH (containing FAD)**, transferring electrons directly to **Ubiquinone (CoQ)**—**bypassing Complex I** and yielding only **1.5 ATP** per cytosolic NADH!
csir_high_yield: Complete Modern CSIR NET ATP Accounting per 1 Molecule of Glucose ($2.5\ \text{ATP/NADH}$ and $1.5\ \text{ATP/FADH}_2$):
• **1. Glycolysis (in Cytosol)**:
– Substrate-level phosphorylation: $+2\ \text{ATP}$ net ($4$ made $-$ $2$ spent).
– $2\ \text{Cytosolic NADH}$: Yields **$5\ \text{ATP}$** (via Malate-Aspartate shuttle) OR **$3\ \text{ATP}$** (via Glycerol-3-P shuttle).
• **2. Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex (in Matrix, $2\ \text{Pyruvate} \rightarrow 2\ \text{Acetyl-CoA}$)**:
– $2\ \text{Matrix NADH} \times 2.5 = \mathbf{5\ \text{ATP}}$.
• **3. TCA Cycle (in Matrix, $2\ \text{Turns}$)**:
– $6\ \text{Matrix NADH} \times 2.5 = \mathbf{15\ \text{ATP}}$.
– $2\ \text{FADH}_2 \times 1.5 = \mathbf{3\ \text{ATP}}$.
– $2\ \text{GTP (ATP)}$ (substrate-level at Succinyl-CoA synthetase) $= \mathbf{2\ \text{ATP}}$.

• **GRAND TOTAL**: **$32\ \text{ATP}$** (Liver/Heart/Kidney) or **$30\ \text{ATP}$** (Skeletal Muscle/Brain)! *(Note: In bacteria, which lack mitochondria and require zero shuttle transport, 1 Glucose also yields 32 ATP!).*

• **Where is the ONLY Membrane-Bound Enzyme of the TCA Cycle?** **Succinate Dehydrogenase (Complex II)** is embedded directly in the Inner Mitochondrial Membrane; all other 7 TCA enzymes are soluble in the matrix!

node_thermodynamics_redox.subtitle: $\Delta G'^\circ = -nF\Delta E'^\circ$, Coupled Endergonic/Exergonic Reactions & Why ATP Hydrolysis Yields $-50\ \text{kJ/mol}$ In Vivo

metrics.gibbs_free_energy_eq: ΔG = ΔG'° + RT × ln( [Products] / [Reactants] ) | At Equilibrium (ΔG = 0): ΔG'° = -RT × ln(K'_eq) = -2.303 RT log10(K'_eq)
metrics.rt_constant_25c: At 25°C (298 K): RT = 2.48 kJ/mol (0.59 kcal/mol) and 2.303 RT = 5.706 kJ/mol (1.36 kcal/mol)!
metrics.redox_free_energy_eq: ΔG'° = -n × F × ΔE'° [where n = electrons transferred, F = Faraday constant = 96.485 kJ/(V·mol), ΔE'° = E'°(Acceptor) - E'°(Donor)]

mechanism: **1. RELATING BIOCHEMICAL EQUILIBRIUM CONSTANT ($K'_{\text{eq}}$) TO $\Delta G'^\circ$ AT pH 7.0 ($25^\circ\text{C}$)**:
$$\Delta G'^\circ = -2.303\ RT \log_{10}(K'_{\text{eq}}) = -5.7\ \text{kJ/mol} \times \log_{10}(K'_{\text{eq}})$$
• Every **10-fold increase in $K'_{\text{eq}}$** makes $\Delta G'^\circ$ more negative by exactly **$-5.7\ \text{kJ/mol}$** ($-1.36\ \text{kcal/mol}$):
– $K'_{\text{eq}} = 1 \Longleftrightarrow \Delta G'^\circ = 0\ \text{kJ/mol}$.

– $K'_{\text{eq}} = 10^1 \Longleftrightarrow \Delta G'^\circ = -5.7\ \text{kJ/mol}$ | $K'_{\text{eq}} = 10^2 \Longleftrightarrow \Delta G'^\circ = -11.4\ \text{kJ/mol}$ | $K'_{\text{eq}} = 10^{-3} \Longleftrightarrow \Delta G'^\circ = +17.1\ \text{kJ/mol}$!
**2. REDOX POTENTIAL LADDER ($E'^\circ$) & FREE ENERGY ($\Delta G'^\circ = -nF\Delta E'^\circ$)**:

• Spontaneous electron flow ALWAYS proceeds from the redox couple with the **MORE NEGATIVE reduction potential ($E'^\circ$, stronger reducing agent / electron donor)** to the couple with the **MORE POSITIVE reduction potential ($E'^\circ$, stronger oxidizing agent / electron acceptor)**:
$$\Delta E'^\circ = E'^\circ_{\text{electron acceptor}} - E'^\circ_{\text{electron donor}} > 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \Delta G'^\circ = -nF\Delta E'^\circ < 0$$
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Unit 1 Numerical Problems on Actual $\Delta G$ vs. Standard $\Delta G'^\circ$ & Phosphoryl Group Transfer:

• **1. Why can a Reaction with a POSITIVE $\Delta G'^\circ$ (like Malate $\rightarrow$ Oxaloacetate in the TCA cycle, $\Delta G'^\circ = +29.7\ \text{kJ/mol}$, or Aldolase in Glycolysis, $\Delta G'^\circ = +23.8\ \text{kJ/mol}$) Proceed Forward Spontaneously Inside a Living Cell?**

– Because spontaneity in vivo is determined by the **ACTUAL Free Energy Change ($\Delta G$)**, NOT $\Delta G'^\circ$! In the mitochondrial matrix, Citrate Synthase continuously consumes Oxaloacetate, keeping the actual mass-action ratio $[\text{OAA}]/[\text{Malate}] < 10^{-6}$ so that $RT\ln Q$ is strongly negative ($<-34\ \text{kJ/mol}$), making actual **$\Delta G < 0$**!
• **2. Ranking of Standard Free Energy of Hydrolysis ($\Delta G'^\circ$) of Phosphorylated Compounds (Who Can Phosphorylate ADP to ATP?)**:
1. **Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)**: **$-61.9\ \text{kJ/mol}$** (Highest! Driven by enol-to-keto tautomerization of pyruvate).
2. **1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (1,3-BPG)**: **$-49.3\ \text{kJ/mol}$** (Resonance stabilization of 3-PGA).
3. **Phosphocreatine**: **$-43.0\ \text{kJ/mol}$**.
4. **ATP ($\rightarrow$ ADP + $\text{P}_i$)**: **$-30.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$** (Actual cellular $\Delta G_p \approx -50\text{ to }-54\ \text{kJ/mol}$!).
5. **Glucose-1-Phosphate**: **$-20.9\ \text{kJ/mol}$** | **Glucose-6-Phosphate**: **$-13.8\ \text{kJ/mol}$** | **Glycerol-3-Phosphate**: **$-9.2\ \text{kJ/mol}$**.

*Rule*: Only compounds **ABOVE ATP** ($\text{PEP}$, $1,3\text{-BPG}$, Phosphocreatine, Succinyl-CoA) have a more negative $\Delta G'^\circ$ than $-30.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$ and can drive **Substrate-Level Phosphorylation of ADP $\rightarrow$ ATP**!

node_complex_i_nadh.title: Complex I (NADH : Ubiquinone Oxidoreductase — 45 Subunits, ~1 MDa)
node_complex_i_nadh.subtitle: L-Shaped Proton Pump: NADH -> FMN -> 7–8 Fe-S Clusters (N2) -> Ubiquinone (CoQ10) | Pumps 4 H+ / 2 e-

metrics.prosthetic_pathway: Matrix NADH (2e- hydride) -> FMN (2e- to 1e- transducer!) -> 7–8 Fe-S Clusters (N3 -> N1b -> N4 -> N5 -> N6a -> N6b -> N2) -> Ubiquinone (Q -> QH2)
metrics.proton_stoichiometry: Pumps 4 H+ from Matrix to IMS per 2 e- (1 NADH) oxidized!
metrics.classic_inhibitors: Rotenone (Plant isoflavonoid insecticide), Piericidin A, Amytal / Barbiturates, & Demerol (All block electron transfer from Fe-S cluster N2 to Ubiquinone!)

mechanism: **Complex I** is the largest multimeric enzyme of the respiratory chain (**45 subunits in mammals**: 7 hydrophobic core subunits encoded by **mtDNA [*ND1–ND6, ND4L*]** + 38 nuclear-encoded subunits), folded into an **L-shaped architecture**:

1. **Hydrophilic Matrix Arm (Electron Transfer Wire)**: Matrix **NADH** donates a **2-electron hydride ion ($\text{H}^-$)** to **FMN (Flavin Mononucleotide)** ($\rightarrow \text{FMNH}_2$). Because Iron-Sulfur ($\text{Fe-S}$) clusters can only carry **1 electron at a time** ($\text{Fe}^{3+} \leftrightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}$), **FMN acts as an obligate $2e^- \rightarrow 1e^-$ step-down transducer**, passing electrons singly down a wire of 7 conserved $[2\text{Fe-2S}]$ and $[4\text{Fe-4S}]$ clusters culminating in the high-potential cluster **N2**.

2. **Hydrophobic Membrane Arm (Conformational Proton Pump)**: Electron transfer from cluster **N2** to lipid-soluble **Ubiquinone ($\text{CoQ}_{10}$)** (plus $2\text{H}^+$ from the matrix to form **Ubiquinol, $\text{QH}_2$**) drives long-range Electrostatic conformational waves across three antiporter-like subunits (ND2, ND4, ND5) that **pump $4\text{H}^+$ from the Matrix into the Intermembrane Space**!
csir_high_yield: High-Yield CSIR NET Questions on Complex I Inhibitors & Bypass Rescue:

• **Does Complex I contain any Heme (Cytochrome) prosthetic groups?** **NO!** Complex I contains **ONLY FMN and Iron–Sulfur ($\text{Fe-S}$) clusters**! (Hemes appear only in Complex II [$b_{560}$], Complex III [$b_L, b_H, c_1$], and Complex IV [$a, a_3$]).
• **Classic Rotenone + Succinate Rescue Experiment (Guaranteed CSIR Part C Oxygen-Electrode Question!)**:

– Mitochondria respiring on **Pyruvate/Malate or Glutamate/Malate** (which generate **NADH** for Complex I) are treated with **Rotenone (or Amytal)**: Oxygen consumption **drops immediately to ZERO**!

– Now **Succinate** (or Glycerol-3-Phosphate) is added to the exact same Rotenone-poisoned chamber: **Oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis IMMEDIATELY RESUME!** Why? Because Succinate feeds electrons via **Complex II ($\text{FADH}_2$)** directly into the **Ubiquinone ($\text{CoQ}$) pool**, completely **bypassing blocked Complex I**!
pathology: • Maternal mtDNA point mutations in Complex I subunits (*MT-ND1, ND4, ND6*) cause selective degeneration of retinal ganglion cells and adult-onset blindness.
• **Rotenone** and **MPP+ (metabolite of MPTP)** inhibit Complex I in nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons, causing superoxide leakage from FMN and clinical **Parkinson's disease**.

node_complex_ii_sdh.subtitle: 100% Nuclear-Encoded! Succinate -> Covalently Bound FAD -> 3 Fe-S Clusters -> Heme b560 -> Ubiquinone | Pumps 0 H+!

metrics.subunit_genetics: 4 Subunits (SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD): 100% NUCLEAR-ENCODED! (The ONLY respiratory complex with ZERO mtDNA-encoded subunits!)
metrics.prosthetic_pathway: Succinate -> Covalently bound FAD (His-flavinated on SDHA) -> [2Fe-2S] -> [4Fe-4S] -> [3Fe-4S] (on SDHB) -> Ubiquinone (Heme b560 prevents ROS leak)

mechanism: **Complex II (Succinate : Ubiquinone Oxidoreductase)** is the physical and catalytic bridge linking the **TCA Cycle** directly to the **Electron Transport Chain**:
• **SDHA** (matrix-facing flavoprotein) oxidizes **Succinate $\rightarrow$ Fumarate**, reducing a **covalently attached FAD** prosthetic group to $\text{FADH}_2$.

• Electrons pass singly through **three Iron–Sulfur clusters** ($[2\text{Fe-2S}] \rightarrow [4\text{Fe-4S}] \rightarrow [3\text{Fe-4S}]$) in **SDHB** to reduce **Ubiquinone ($\text{CoQ}_{10}$) $\rightarrow \text{QH}_2$** bound at the membrane-anchor subunits **SDHC/SDHD** (which also coordinate a single **Heme $b_{560}$** that acts as an electron sink to prevent superoxide radical formation).
csir_high_yield: Three Guaranteed CSIR NET Exam Facts About Complex II:

• **1. Why does $\text{FADH}_2$ yield only $1.5\ \text{ATP}$ whereas $\text{NADH}$ yields $2.5\ \text{ATP}$?** Because **Complex II pumps ZERO ($0$) protons ($\text{H}^+$)** across the inner mitochondrial membrane! Electrons from $\text{FADH}_2$ enter the Ubiquinone pool and only pump protons at **Complex III ($4\text{H}^+$) + Complex IV ($2\text{H}^+$) = $6\text{H}^+$ total** ($6/4 = \mathbf{1.5\ \text{ATP}}$), whereas NADH pumps $4\text{H}^+$ at Complex I + $4\text{H}^+$ at Complex III + $2\text{H}^+$ at Complex IV $= \mathbf{10\text{H}^+}$ total ($10/4 = \mathbf{2.5\ \text{ATP}}$)!

• **2. Which is the ONLY ETC Complex Encoded 100% by the Nuclear Genome?** **Complex II (SDHA, B, C, D)**! Therefore, in **$\rho^0$ cells (cells completely stripped of mitochondrial DNA by ethidium bromide)**, Complexes I, III, IV, and V are completely absent/non-functional, **WHEREAS Complex II (Succinate Dehydrogenase) remains 100% enzymatically ACTIVE**!

• **3. Malonate vs. Carboxin / TTFA**: **Malonate** ($\text{HOOC–CH}_2\text{–COOH}$) is the textbook **competitive inhibitor** of the Succinate active site on SDHA; **Carboxin** (systemic fungicide) and **TTFA** block electron transfer from the $[3\text{Fe-4S}]$ cluster to Ubiquinone.
pathology: **Hereditary Paraganglioma & Pheochromocytoma (*SDHB / SDHD* Tumor Suppressor Mutations)**: Loss-of-function mutations in *SDH* subunits cause intracellular **Succinate** accumulation. Excess Succinate competitively inhibits $\alpha$-ketoglutarate-dependent **Prolyl Hydroxylases (PHDs)**, stabilizing **HIF-1$\alpha$** under normoxia (**'Pseudohypoxia'**) and inhibiting TET DNA demethylases as an **Oncometabolite**!

node_complex_iii_q_cycle.subtitle: Qo vs. Qi Sites: Why 2 QH2 Oxidized Yield 1 QH2 Regenerated, 2 Cyt c Reduced & 4 H+ Released to IMS

metrics.prosthetic_groups: Cytochrome b (mtDNA-encoded; contains Low-Potential Heme bL & High-Potential Heme bH) + Rieske Iron-Sulfur Protein ([2Fe-2S]) + Cytochrome c1 (Heme c1)
metrics.q_cycle_net_equation: QH2 + 2 Cyt c (Fe3+) + 2 H+_(Matrix) -> Q + 2 Cyt c (Fe2+) + 4 H+_(IMS)!
metrics.mobile_shuttle_out: Cytochrome c (Water-soluble 12.4 kDa peripheral protein on outer IMS face of IMM; carries 1 e- via covalently thioether-linked Heme c!)
metrics.site_specific_inhibitors: Myxothiazol & Stigmatellin (Block outer Qo site!) vs. Antimycin A (Blocks inner Qi site!)

mechanism: **Complex III (Ubiquinol : Cytochrome $c$ Oxidoreductase)** solves a fundamental stoichiometry puzzle: **Ubiquinol ($\text{QH}_2$) is a 2-electron, 2-proton carrier** diffusing inside the lipid bilayer, whereas **Cytochrome $c$ is strictly a 1-electron, 0-proton carrier** in the aqueous Intermembrane Space! It couples this $2e^- \rightarrow 1e^-$ split to proton translocation via **Mitchell's Two-Half-Turn Q-Cycle**:

• **HALF-TURN 1 (At the Outer/IMS-facing $Q_o$ Site)**: The first **$\text{QH}_2$** docks at the **$Q_o$ site** and releases **$2\text{H}^+$ into the IMS**. Its **2 electrons bifurcate (split)** down two different paths:

– **Electron 2 (Low-Potential Recycling Chain)**: Jumps across the membrane through **Heme $b_L \rightarrow$ Heme $b_H$** to the inner/Matrix-facing **$Q_i$ site**, where it reduces an oxidized Ubiquinone ($Q$) into a stable **Semiquinone Radical ($Q^{\bullet -}$)**!

mechanism: **1. PAUL BOYER'S BINDING-CHANGE MECHANISM (1997 Nobel Prize with John Walker)**:

• **The #1 Conceptual Surprise**: On the surface of the $\beta$-subunit in the **Tight ($T$) conformation**, the synthesis of $\text{ATP}$ from $\text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$ has an equilibrium constant **$K'_{\text{eq}} \approx 1.0$ ($\Delta G'^\circ \approx 0$)**—meaning **forming the phosphoanhydride bond of ATP on the enzyme surface requires ZERO proton-motive force**! Instead, the Proton-Motive Force is required to drive the mechanical rotation of the asymmetric **$\gamma$-subunit axle**, which forces the Tight ($T$) $\beta$-subunit into the **Open ($O$) conformation to RELEASE the tightly bound ATP** into the matrix!
• **The 3 Asymmetric States of theThree $\beta$-Subunits at Any Instant**:
– **L (Loose)**: Binds $\text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$ loosely (catalytically inactive).
– **T (Tight)**: Binds $\text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$ so tightly that they spontaneously condense into **tightly bound $\text{ATP}$**.
– **O (Open)**: Very low affinity; **releases newly synthesized $\text{ATP}$** and binds fresh $\text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$.
**2. PROTON-DRIVEN ROTATION OF THE $c$-RING & $\gamma$-AXLE**:

Protons from the IMS enter the entry half-channel of the stationary **$a$-subunit**, neutralize a conserved negatively charged **Glutamate/Aspartate (Glu-58)** on a **$c$-subunit** so it can rotate nearly $360^\circ$ through the hydrophobic lipid bilayer, and exit into the Matrix via the second half-channel of the $a$-subunit (guided by the essential **Arginine** stator charge on subunit $a$).

• **Oligomycin vs. DCCD ($N,N'$-Dicyclohexylcarbodiimide)**:
– **Oligomycin**: Binds at the interface between the **$a$-subunit and $c$-ring of $F_o$** (whence the 'O' in $F_o$ = *Oligomycin-sensitive factor*!).
– **DCCD**: Reacts covalently with the single protonated **Carboxyl side chain (Glutamate/Aspartate)** inside the **$c$-subunit** of $F_o$, locking the $c$-ring rotor!

– Without the $F_o$ membrane proton channel and an intact $\Delta p$, soluble **$F_1$ acts solely as an ATPase** (hydrolyzing $\text{ATP} \rightarrow \text{ADP} + \text{P}_i$)! Only when purified $F_1$ knobs are added back to $F_1$-stripped submitochondrial vesicles is oxidative phosphorylation restored!

mechanism: **1. QUANTITATIVE PROTON-MOTIVE FORCE ($\Delta p$ OR PMF) EQUATION**:

Across the inner mitochondrial membrane, pumping $\text{H}^+$ out of the matrix creates BOTH an **Electrical Potential ($\Delta\Psi \approx 150\text{–}180\ \text{mV}$, Matrix negative)** and a **Chemical pH Gradient ($\Delta\text{pH} = \text{pH}_{\text{IMS}} - \text{pH}_{\text{Matrix}} \approx 7.2 - 8.0 = -0.8\ \text{units}$, Matrix alkaline)**:
$$\Delta p\ (\text{mV}) = \Delta\Psi - 59\ \Delta\text{pH} \qquad \Longleftrightarrow \qquad \Delta G_{\text{H}^+} = -F\Delta p \approx -20\ \text{kJ/mol H}^+$$
**2. WHY EXPORTING 1 ATP TO THE CYTOSOL COSTS 1 EXTRA PROTON ($3 + 1 = 4\ \text{H}^+$)**:

• **Adenine Nucleotide Translocase (ANT, the most abundant protein in the IMM!)** exchanges **Matrix $\text{ATP}^{4-}$ (4 negative charges) OUT** for **Cytosolic $\text{ADP}^{3-}$ (3 negative charges) IN**. Because exporting one net negative charge out of the negative matrix is driven by $\Delta\Psi$, it is coupled to **Phosphate Translocase**, which imports **$1\ \text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- + 1\ \text{H}^+$** into the matrix (**consuming $1\text{H}^+$ of the proton-motive force**!).

• Combining $\sim 3\text{H}^+$ (for $120^\circ$ rotation of $F_oF_1$) $+\ 1\text{H}^+$ (for $\text{P}_i/\text{ATP}$ transport) $= \mathbf{4\text{H}^+\text{ per cytosolic ATP}}$! Since NADH pumps $10\text{H}^+$, **$10 / 4 = \mathbf{2.5\ \text{ATP/NADH}}$**; since $\text{FADH}_2$ pumps $6\text{H}^+$, **$6 / 4 = \mathbf{1.5\ \text{ATP/FADH}_2}$**!

– **Bongkrekic Acid** (*Burkholderia cocovenenans* fermented-coconut toxin): Binds ANT from the **Matrix face (m-state)**, locking ANT facing inward.

mechanism: Unlike mammalian mitochondria, **Plant, Fungal, and Trypanosome Mitochondria** possess a branched respiratory chain containing two energy-dissipating bypasses:

1. **ALTERNATIVE OXIDASE (AOX — Cyanide-Resistant Respiration)**: A homodimeric interfacial membrane protein containing a **non-heme di-iron ($\text{Fe–Fe}$) center** (activated via pyruvate binding and thioredoxin disulfide reduction). **AOX takes electrons directly from Ubiquinol ($\text{QH}_2$) and reduces $\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$ in a single step—completely bypassing Complex III, Cytochrome $c$, and Complex IV**!

2. **TYPE II ROTENONE-INSENSITIVE NAD(P)H DEHYDROGENASES ($\text{ND}_{\text{ex}}$ and $\text{ND}_{\text{in}}$)**: Single-subunit flavoproteins on both the IMS and Matrix surfaces of the plant IMM that transfer electrons from cytosolic or matrix $\text{NADH/NADPH}$ to Ubiquinone without pumping protons (**bypassing Complex I**!).

**COMBINED ENERGETIC CONSEQUENCE**: If electrons enter via $\text{ND}_{\text{in/ex}}$ ($0\ \text{H}^+$) and exit via **AOX** ($0\ \text{H}^+$), **ZERO protons are pumped and ZERO ATP is made**, allowing the TCA cycle to keep producing carbon skeletons ($\alpha$-ketoglutarate) and preventing over-reduction/ROS damage when cellular ATP is already full!

• **Why Do Isolated Plant Mitochondria Continue Consuming $\text{O}_2$ After Adding Potassium Cyanide ($\text{KCN}$) or Azide ($\text{NaN}_3$)?**

– Because **AOX is 100% INSENSITIVE to Cyanide, Azide, Antimycin A, and Carbon Monoxide**! When Complex IV is blocked by KCN, electrons in the Ubiquinol ($\text{QH}_2$) pool divert through **AOX** to $\text{O}_2$!
• **How Do You Completely Stop Plant Mitochondrial $\text{O}_2$ Consumption?**
– You must add **BOTH KCN** (to block the Cytochrome Complex IV pathway) **AND SHAM (Salicylhydroxamic Acid** or *n*-propyl gallate, to block the **Alternative Oxidase [AOX]** pathway)!
• **Thermogenic Pollination in Araceae (*Symplocarpus foetidus* [Skunk Cabbage] & *Sauromatum guttatum* [Voodoo Lily])**:

– Just before flowering, **Salicylic Acid** triggers a massive surge in **AOX** and **$\text{ND}_{\text{in}}$** expression in the floral **spadix**; uncoupled oxidation of starch via AOX heats the spadix **$15\text{–}25^\circ\text{C}$ above ambient freezing air temperature** to volatilize foul-smelling amines/indoles and attract carrion-beetle pollinators!
pathology: **African Sleeping Sickness (*Trypanosoma brucei*) Trypanosome Alternative Oxidase (TAO)**: Bloodstream-form *Trypanosoma brucei* lacks cytochromes (Complexes III and IV) and relies **100% on a Glycerol-3-Phosphate Shuttle coupled to Trypanosome Alternative Oxidase (TAO)** to re-oxidize glycolytic NADH—making TAO inhibitors (**Ascofuranone** and **SHAM + Glycerol**) selectively lethal to the parasite!
lab_workbench: $^{18}\text{O}_2 / ^{16}\text{O}_2$ Isotope Fractionation Mass Spectrometry for In Vivo AOX Flux Partitioning: Even without adding inhibitors, **AOX discriminates much more strongly against heavy $^{18}\text{O}_2$ ($\sim 24\text{–}30\text{‰}$) than Cytochrome $c$ Oxidase ($\sim 18\text{‰}$)**, allowing exact non-invasive quantification of in vivo electron partitioning between Complex IV and AOX in intact leaves!
